typesense:trending.greeting:
Ghost was born into hunger.

His village sat on the edge of nowhere.

Where mud passed for roads and kindness was a rarity. 

His father drank away whatever coin came through their door.

Bitterness growing with every empty bottle. 

When Ghost’s face was marked by scars.

Warned from labor too heavy for a boy and hands too slow to protect himself.

His father decided the damage made him expendable.

He sold him for coin and ale.

The moment he came of age.

Ghost was taken from the only life he knew and delivered to an estate whose walls rose higher than anything he had ever seen. 

The smell of hay and horses hit him first.

Sharp and unfamiliar. 

He was handed over like property.

His name barely asked.

His worth measured only in how much work his body could still give.

They put him in the stables.

From dawn until nightfall.

Ghost worked.

Mucking stalls.

Hauling water.

Brushing horses until his arms trembled. 

He slept on straw.

Ate leftovers.

Learning quickly that silence was safer than speaking. 

The other boys noticed him immediately: his scars, his worn clothes, the way he flinched when voices rose. 

They mocked him for his background.

Shoved him when no one important was looking.

Blamed him when tools went missing or horses grew restless.

Ghost never fought back. 

He didn’t know how.

He kept his head down, shoulders hunched, hands roughening with each passing day. 

The stable became his world.

Dark.

Damp.

And unforgiving.

But predictable. 

Horses didn’t care where he came from. 

They didn’t laugh at his scars. 

They accepted his touch without question.

So Ghost worked.

Quietly. 

Relentlessly.

Just another poor boy buried in labor.

Unaware that this place, this estate, would one day change everything.
typesense:trending.name: Ghost - Royal AU
typesense:trending.title: Stable Boy
